sources.title: Constitution of Tonga, 2020 Revised Edition

claims.text: Clauses 30 and 41 describe a constitutional monarchy; royal signature is required for legislation. Clause 36 assigns military command to the King but requires Assembly consent for war.

The King appoints the Assembly-recommended elected representative as prime minister. Cabinet exercises executive authority collectively and answers to the Assembly; ministers are nominated by the prime minister and appointed by the King. Reserved royal powers are excluded.
The King appoints Privy Council advisers. The Council also handles specified hereditary estate and title appeals.
The Assembly includes nobles' representatives, people's representatives and Cabinet. Its recommended Speaker must be an elected nobles' representative and is appointed by the King.

sources.scope_note: Consolidated edition, not a complete amendment or commencement ledger. Do not backdate these provisions to 1990 or assume no later amendments.

sources.title: Act of Constitution of Tonga, older revised text

claims.text: The older text gives the King appointment of ministers, serving at his pleasure or for their commission period. Ministers sit in the Privy Council and Assembly.
The older text includes Privy Councillors and Cabinet in the Assembly, specifies nine noble and nine people's elected representatives, and gives the King appointment of the Speaker.

sources.scope_note: The volume carries a 1988 Revised Edition label but includes later amendment notes, including Act 12 of 1990. It is not accepted as an exact 1 January 1990 legal snapshot.

The printed Act records Assembly passage on 20 July 2010. Passage alone does not establish commencement.

Siaosi Sovaleni, submitted by Hon. Dr 'Aisake Eke (Tongatapu 5) together with the motion, signed in support by 10 Members including Eke, and that the Office was acting as required by clause 50B of the Constitution.

sources.title: Ko e Miniti 'o e Feme'a'aki 'a e Hou'eiki Mēmipa 'o e Fale Alea 'o Tonga, Fika 48, 'Aho Mōnite 9 Tīsema 2024 (Minutes No. 48, Monday 9 December 2024)

claims.text: The minutes of sitting No. 48 (Monday 9 December 2024), whose agenda listed Motion No. 4A/2024 for a vote of no confidence in the Prime Minister and the Prime Minister's written reply, record Prime Minister Siaosi Sovaleni ('Eiki Palēmia) announcing in the House, under the heading 'Fakafisi 'Eiki Palēmia mei he lakanga Palēmia 'o Tonga', that he resigns as Prime Minister of Tonga 'Fakatatau ki he Konisitūtoné Kupu 50 (2)(c), effective immediately he 'ahó ni' (in accordance with clause 50(2)(c), effective immediately today), and taking leave of the Deputy Prime Minister and Cabinet.
claims.locator: PDF p.3 (agenda items 4.1-4.2); PDF pp.40-41 (heading; time blocks 1150-1155 and 1155-1200)
claims.uncertainty: The clause is printed '50 (2)(c)'; the Speaker later cites clause 50(a)(2)(c). The printed form is kept and not corrected. The time of day is bracketed only by the transcript's five-minute blocks. The resignation letter itself, and the date on which it was written or signed, are not in the minutes. The Speaker relied on His Majesty's written reply, not on these words, for confirmation (to_speaker_vonc_withdrawn_procedure_20241209).

claims.text: The same minutes record the Table Clerk reading, in the 1400-1405 block after the House resumed, a letter from the Palace Office dated Monday 9 December 2024, signed by Sione U. Fifita, Secretary to His Majesty, and addressed to Speaker Lord Fakafanua: the Palace Office had received that day, Monday 9 December 2024, Hon. Hu'akavameiliku's letter to King Tupou VI resigning as Prime Minister of Tonga, and His Majesty had graciously accepted the resignation ('Kuo mokoi 'a e Finangalo 'a 'Ene 'Afió ki he fakafisi').
claims.locator: PDF p.42: Speaker's adjournment to 2pm at the top of the page; 1400-1405 block, heading 'Tohi mei he 'Ofisi Palasi fekau'aki mo e Tohi Fakafisi Palēmia 'o Tonga'
claims.uncertainty: The Palace letter is known only as read into the minutes; the original and the resignation letter are not published. The minutes bracket the acceptance: the resignation was announced in the 1150-1200 block; the Speaker then said the matter was to be completed with His Majesty under the Constitution and adjourned the House to 2pm; at 1400-1405 he said the recess had been used to convey it to His Majesty ('Na'a tau ngāue'aki aipē 'a e taimi mālōlō ke fakahoko eni ki he 'Ene 'Afio') and that the Palace letter had then reached his Office. Acceptance therefore fell within that recess on 9 December; its clock time is not recorded.

claims.text: The Speaker then removed agenda items 4.1 and 4.2 (the no-confidence motion and the Prime Minister's reply), ruled that both documents be released as public records of the Assembly although not tabled, and stated that because the office of Prime Minister was vacant the Schedule under clause 50(A) applied: invitations within 10 days, counted from the next day; 14 days for nominations, expected to end on Monday 23 December; and a meeting within 3 days, to be held on 24 December, to which he adjourned the House. He also read clause 50(a)(2)(c) (a Prime Minister holds office until death, resignation or revocation of appointment) and stated that the resignation had been confirmed that day by His Majesty's written reply ('tohi tali mei he 'Ene 'Afió').
claims.locator: PDF p.43 (end of the 1400-1405 block: items 4.1-4.2 removed and public-record ruling; 1405-1410 block: the Schedule); p.46 (1410-1415: clause 50(a)(2)(c) read; 1415-1420: confirmation by His Majesty's reply); p.50 (adjournment to 24 Tīsema)
claims.uncertainty: Procedural statements by the Speaker in debate. No vote on the motion took place; this is a clause 50A vacancy, not a clause 50B removal.

claims.text: Answering Lord Tu'ivakanō's request that the King be asked for an interim Cabinet ('Kapineti fakataimi') during the 14-day period, the Speaker had section 18(2) of the Government Act read (the Deputy Prime Minister exercises the powers and performs the duties of the Prime Minister when the Prime Minister cannot act because of absence, illness or other reason) and ruled that on a resignation under clause 50(a) the existing Cabinet remains and, under the Government Act, the Deputy Prime Minister acts ('Le'ole'o leva 'a e 'Eiki Tokoni Palēmiá'); he found no constitutional power for the King to remove the Cabinet short of dissolving the Assembly, the Cabinet leaving office under the Constitution only when the Prime Minister is removed under clause 50(b).
claims.locator: PDF pp.47-50 (headings 'Tokanga Nōpele Tongatapu 2 ke 'omai ha Kapineti Fakataimi ...'; 1420-1430 blocks)
claims.uncertainty: The Speaker's ruling in debate, not an instrument appointing an Acting Prime Minister. It names no person and dates no start. The Government Act was not retrieved; section 18(2) is taken only as read into the minutes. Ha'apai 13 cites an earlier precedent of a Prime Minister's death, which is not imported.

claims.text: The members' list printed at the front of the same minutes ('Hou'eiki Minisitā Kapineti') sets Hon. Samiu Vaipulu against ''Eiki Tokoni Palēmia, 'Eiki Minisitā Lao & Pilīsone' (Deputy Prime Minister; Justice and Prisons), Hon. Siaosi Sovaleni against ''Eiki Palēmia' with Education & Training and Police & Fire Services, and Hon. Tiofilusi Tiueti against Finance & National Planning and Revenue & Customs. It says nothing about acting office.

sources.title: Ko e Miniti 'o e Fili Palēmia Fili 'a e Hou'eiki Mēmipa 'o e Fale Alea 'o Tonga, Tūsite 24 Tīsema 2024 (Minutes of the election of the Prime Minister Designate)

claims.text: The minutes of the special meeting of Elected Representatives on Tuesday 24 December 2024 record the Speaker describing it as a special meeting under the Schedule to clause 50(a), not an ordinary sitting, held because the office of Prime Minister became vacant on the resignation of the former Prime Minister, Hon. Hu'akavameiliku, on 9 December 2024. Two sealed nominations were opened: No. 1, dated 18 December 2024 and received on 20 December 2024 at 3:48pm, nominating 'Aisake Valu 'Eke (proposer 'Uhilamoelangi Fasi; seconders Taniela Liku'ohihifo Fusimālohi and Mo'ale Finau); No. 2, dated 23 December 2024 and received on 23 December 2024 at 12.00 noon, nominating Hon. Dr. Viliami Uasikē Lātū, Vava'u 16 (proposer Hon. Dr. Mo'ale 'Otunuku; seconders Hon. Sevenitini Toumoua and Hon. Vātau Mefi Hui). The Clerk confirmed both as complete.
claims.locator: PDF pp.8-9 (Speaker's address); pp.11-13 ('Tohi Fika 1', 'Tohi Fika 2')
claims.uncertainty: Proposers and seconders are nomination roles, not party or coalition membership.

claims.text: The same minutes record that, in the 1500-1505 block after the secret ballot, the Speaker stated he had completed his duty of reporting the Assembly's election result to His Majesty the King and then announced the result of the secret ballot of Tuesday 24 December 2024: 24 votes in all, a majority being 13; Hon. 'Aisake Valu Eke 16, Hon. Viliami Uasikē Lātū 8; Eke, Tongatapu 5, elected with 16 votes. The result was read by the Clerk of the Assembly, Gloria Pōle'o, and confirmed by Sefita Tangi, Auditor General. The Speaker closed by adjourning to the new year and leaving to the Prime Minister-elect the remaining business of forming his Cabinet.
claims.locator: PDF pp.52-53 ('Fakahā e ola 'o e Fili Fakapulipuli Fili Palēmia'); p.55
claims.uncertainty: This is the Assembly's selection of the Prime Minister Designate under clause 50A, not the royal appointment or a start of office. The report to the King precedes the announcement in the record; its exact time is not given.

claims.text: At the same meeting the Speaker's address, Lātū's candidate speech and Eke's candidate speech each include the Acting Prime Minister (''Eiki Palēmia Le'ole'o') in their salutations; Lātū's also greets the acting members of the Cabinet ('Hou'eiki Mēmipa Le'ole'o 'o e Kapineti') and Eke's the Cabinet ('Hou'eiki Kapinetí'). None of these salutations names the Acting Prime Minister.
claims.locator: PDF p.9 (Me'a 'a e 'Eiki Seá); p.19 (Fakamalanga Vava'u 16, 1105-1110 block); p.13 (Fakamalanga Tongatapu 5)
claims.uncertainty: A form of address only; no name, instrument or start date. The Speaker's later call to the Acting Prime Minister is a separate claim (to_acting_pm_vaipulu_floor_20241224).

claims.text: In the 1320-1325 block of the same minutes the Speaker, with only Vava'u members left to speak, gives the floor with 'me'a mai Palēmia Le'ole'o' (the Acting Prime Minister has the floor); the speech that follows is headed 'Fakamalanga poupou Vava'u 15 kia Viliami Uasikē Lātū' (Vava'u 15's speech supporting Lātū) and carries the speaker label Samiu Vaipulu. The roll of Elected Representatives at the front of the minutes prints 'Samiu Kuita Vaipulu - Fakafofonga Kakai Vāhenga Fili Vava'u 15'.
claims.locator: PDF p.47 (1320-1325 block); p.3 (roll of Elected Representatives)
claims.uncertainty: The Speaker's form of address in debate, not an appointing instrument. It identifies the member called on as Acting Prime Minister on 24 December 2024 but gives no start date, instrument or end, and 9 December is not inferred from it. Page 47 was read from the pypdfium2 text layer only; page 3 was rendered.

sources.scope_note: Tongan-language verbatim minutes (55-page PDF, created 3 February 2025) of the special meeting of Elected Representatives on 24 December 2024, downloaded through the Phoca Download button on the file page. The 4 March 2025 listing date is the upload date, not the meeting date. English renderings are this packet's reading, not an official translation.

sources.title: Public Announcement: 'Current Status of His Majesty's Government' (Fanongonongo ki he Kakai: 'Tu'unga 'o e Pule'anga 'o 'Ene 'Afio'), 6 January 2025
sources.publisher: Government of Tonga, Prime Minister's Office

claims.text: The Government of Tonga Public Announcement dated 6 January 2025, 'Current Status of His Majesty's Government' (with the Tongan 'Tu'unga 'o e Pule'anga 'o 'Ene 'Afio' of the same date), states that Government resumed work that day, Monday 6 January 2025; that it is in 'caretaker mode' ('tauhi fakataimi') under the Acting Prime Minister ('Palēmia Le'ole'o'), Hon. Samiu Kuita Vaipulu, and the current Cabinet Ministers; that no new financial commitments or policies are to be made in the caretaker period; and that the caretaker Government continues until the appointment of Prime Minister Designate Hon. Dr. 'Aisake Valu Eke and of his new Cabinet Ministers is completed, after which the appointments of the current Cabinet Ministers will be revoked.
claims.locator: Image 1 (English), date line and paragraphs 1-5 and 7; image 2 (Tongan), paragraphs 1-5
claims.uncertainty: Attests the arrangement on 6 January 2025. It does not say when Vaipulu began acting, under what instrument, or when the caretaker period ended; the revocation of the current ministers is a forecast, not a dated act. Its final paragraph says the Office of the Prime Minister will issue a Public Announcement in due course of the commencement of the New Government; no such announcement was identified.

sources.scope_note: The announcement is published only as two JPEG images (English 1.jpg, Tongan 2.jpg), still served live. The post page now returns HTTP 404, as does its REST endpoint; it was read from a Wayback Machine capture of the original page (26 January 2025), which embeds both images. The capture is an archive of the PMO page, not a PMO-served copy. The coat of arms is not used.

sources.title: His Majesty King Tupou VI appoints Hon. Dr. 'Aisake Valu Eke as Prime Minister of Tonga
sources.publisher: Government of Tonga, Prime Minister's Office

claims.text: The PMO release datelined 'Nuku'alofa, 22 January, 2025' states that King Tupou VI, 'today, Wednesday 22 January 2025, at the Royal Palace, Nuku'alofa', appointed Honourable Dr. 'Aisake Valu Eke 'as the Prime Minister Tonga' (as printed; the title reads 'Prime Minister of Tonga') in accordance with Clause 50A (1) of the Act of the Constitution of Tonga, and describes him as the 19th Prime Minister.
claims.uncertainty: An appointment event. The release gives no separate 'with effect from' date, no warrant signature or presentation, no time and no instrument number. The ordinal is recorded as printed and is not used to number a succession.

claims.text: The same release states that Eke was elected Prime Minister Designate at the Legislative Assembly of Tonga on 24 December 2024 and is the Member of Parliament for Tongatapu No. 5.
claims.uncertainty: Independent PMO corroboration of the Assembly selection; it is not the appointment. The release's biography (birth date, career, family) is not imported.

sources.scope_note: The live post returns HTTP 404 (a Wayback capture of 18 January 2026 also records a 404). claims.text: The minutes of sitting No. 1 of 2025 (Friday 31 January 2025, from 11:00am) record the Chief Clerk administering to the Prime Minister, 'Aisake Valu Eke, the oath 'i he 'ao 'o e Fale Alea 'o Tongá' under clause 83 of the Constitution, taken as 'Palēmia 'o Tonga ka ko e Minisitā Pa'anga, Minisitā ki he Toutaí, Minisitā ki he Pilīsoné' (Prime Minister, Minister of Finance, of Fisheries and of Prisons); he kissed the Bible and signed the oath, which Speaker Lord Fakafanua countersigned. 2021 transition (TO-REC-10; tonga-transition-2021-02.md): the Assembly procedure and 15 December selection, the royal appointment effective 27 December (PMO releases dated 28 December) and the Cabinet effective 28 December are separately sourced (TO-TR21-01 to TO-TR21-03, TO-TR21-06); none of these dates is merged into another.

TO-TR21-04: the signature and presentation dates of the Royal Warrant appointing Siaosi Sovaleni are not recorded in any retrieved primary source; the 28 December release date is not a signature date. A secondary news account of a 28 December presentation is a search lead only.

TO-TR21-05: the end of Pohiva Tu'i'onetoa's premiership and any caretaker or interim boundary before 27 December 2021 are unsourced; no end date is inferred from Sovaleni's effective start. PMO site searches for 'Sovaleni' (result pages 1-2), 'caretaker' (no results), 'Tuionetoa' and 'Pohiva Tu' (no December 2021 record), plus the Assembly news archive, press releases and Hansard index, were checked; no online Government Gazette was located.

2024-2025 transition (tonga-transition-2024-03.md): Siaosi Sovaleni's resignation, announced 'effective immediately' and accepted by the King on 9 December 2024 (TO-TR24-01), the Assembly's selection of 'Aisake Valu Eke on 24 December 2024 by 16 votes to 8 (TO-TR24-03) and his royal appointment under Clause 50A(1) on 22 January 2025 (TO-TR24-04) are separately sourced; none of these dates is merged into another.
